about: The invariants worth drawing: each is a rule the code enforces (a validator, a refusal, a test), grouped by what it protects. These are the labels on the arrows and the locks on the boxes.
authority: CLAUDE.md Rules; each rule names where it is enforced

groups.title: A person's authority is code, not policy

rules.rule: Release approval, scheduling, go-live, paid links, topic approval, unpublishing, retraction, article correction and music clearance are a person's acts; the verbs refuse an automated: actor.
rules.where: publish approve|go-live|decide, topics approve|reject, article correct, links cta approve

rules.rule: Only draft review is configurable (review.draft: person | shadow | agent); an agent may accept or send back a draft, never a release.
Every automated step is a CLI verb a person can run by hand; the manual workflow stays documented and rehearsed.

Every automation flag is off by default; a person verifies an integration against the real service (readiness.json) before enabling it; a passing suite never writes a verification and a verification never changes a flag.
Scheduled tasks, power settings and the mailbox are the person's acts, never a run's.

An agent writes only the files its role grants (scripts, reviews, batches, proposals, components where the graphics brief says); never code outside those paths, configuration, settings or package.json; never a publish, post, push or secret.
rules.where: roles.ts grantFor, DENIED_BASE, the tree guard

rules.rule: A writer and its reviewer are different agents; approvals are by sentence fingerprint, so a changed sentence is re-reviewed.
Every agent artifact is checked by a deterministic validator that fails closed; findings go back to the agent for a bounded number of rounds.
rules.where: script -- validate, topics -- validate, evidence -- check-batch, runs.validationRounds

rules.rule: A writer pass has three revisions to clear its blocking findings; past that, revision-limit stops /produce and only a person's generation.corrective entry goes on.

Containment is protection, not isolation: unauthorised writes are detected and reverted and secrets stay out of agent processes, but agent-written code runs with the user's privileges, so unattended automation stays off until a person turns it on.
A verdict on a claim counts for every source that makes it; adding a source never needs re-judging old claims.
rules.where: the store: topics.json claims, videos/*.json sources

rules.rule: An AI guess counts for at most 0.5 confidence; a study verdict overrides it only when at least as confident; an AI guess never counts as verification; contextual evidence never decides.
Canonical claim text is one line, mechanism-level, no numbers that belong to one source; no personal data (the store is public).
Never hand-edit the store; only npm run record, record-sources, merge-claims and the watcher write it; passages enter the corpus only through record-sources.
A factual sentence needs an assertion per claim it makes; figures, quotations and calculations trace to a cited passage; a script says each thing once.
record-sources refuses a new verdict on a claim and document a script cites unless --replace-cited, which /produce never passes.
The fiction never touches the evidence: the disclosure appears once per surface; no in-world mark may claim more than the verdicts do.

groups.title: State is files in the repo, derived at read

rules.rule: No database, queue, event bus, distributed orchestrator, stored workflow state machine, generic agent framework or generic publishing framework.

stories.json, shorts.json, validation.json, article.md, timeline, mix.json, review/ are derived: never hand-edited, byte-identical on a rerun; judgment lives only in *-review.json keyed by stable ids.
A decision carries who, when and the sha of what it binds: an approval binds the build (mp4 sha) and the composed title; a request binds releaseSha; a changed title or manifest asks again.
publish.json is the one append-only record of what publishing adds; its events are written only by npm run publish; a live video is never replaced.
public-record.json is written only by npm run report and article -- correct; every revision needs a note; a public URL never disappears (public-urls.json, moved.json).
rules.where: public-record.ts, links -- freeze, the build test

rules.rule: Operational files (run/, .automation/) are gitignored and decide no stage; production.json holds queued and parked only.

groups.title: Module boundaries are a compiler-backed test

rules.rule: A capability is a module (index.ts, cli.ts, briefs/, tests/, README.md); a new capability is a new module, never a folder inside another or a home in src/shared/.

A capability never imports another's code, only src/shared/ and src/config/, and reads another's files through shared io; cross-module imports are only index.ts names listed in readApi; the read-API graph is acyclic; the exception list is empty and only shrinks.

Orchestration owns coordination only (derived state, routing, scheduling, execution, retries, budgets, notifications); it never judges content and never writes a module's artifact except through that module's CLI as a child process.

A module exposes validate(...) and inspect(topic, story) -> missing | invalid | stale | ready with no workflow vocabulary; only the board maps an inspection to a halt kind and a next command. Publishing's OutputStep is the one named-verb exception.
Topic discovery is separate from evidence; publishing (YouTube) from social (X); article (editorial text) from website (rendering); institution, topic and story stay distinct.
Find the repo root through ROOT in src/shared/io.ts, never process.cwd(); TOPICS and any join(..., 'topics', ...) live only in io.ts.

groups.title: Secrets stay outside git and outside agents

rules.rule: Secrets live in the gitignored .env and .secrets/, never in the repo, a journal, an attempt record or an event.
The runner hands each child only its verb's secret family and strips every secret from an agent's environment; every role is denied Read(.env) and Read(.secrets/**).
upload refuses before any byte unless the authenticated channel is the commission's; upload never sends anything but private; a lost upload session stops and asks.
Request ids in approval mails are signed with APPROVAL_SECRET; a reply is applied once by thread and request id.

groups.title: The public site shows only what is live

rules.rule: Only topics an institution claims and, in them, only stories with a live video are built; the dev server previews packaged stories; the fixture topic is never paged in production.
Every link to a page is built from a content-graph node id, never a title; href() respects Astro's base.
The site loads nothing from a third party; the admin pages exist only in dev; client JS is a short closed list.
A change to a public page ends with npm run quality (RESULT: PASSED); an exception names one rule, a narrow pattern and a reason; passing is never reported as WCAG conformance.
Every video draws from its institution's kit through theme (no literal colour, no ad hoc mark); a packaged build whose look is not the current one halts look-stale and is never approved.
